Definition: Overall cohort: 152 genomes. Primary reference-group comparisons: 144 genomes (23 subflava, 114 perflava, 7 flavescens). Eight species-unresolved genomes are descriptive only.
RGI 6.0.3 / CARD 4.0.2 Perfect or Strict calls; Loose calls excluded. tet(M) additionally requires >=95% reference length coverage. All 152 genomes had usable outputs.

All 57 mapped tet(M)-related loci from 38 carriers are retained, including five short fragments excluded from sequence-type analysis. Coordinates are 0-based, half-open, in the corresponding assembly contigs.
H01-H07 label seven nucleotide sequences among 52 full-length records in a 1,935-nt alignment. tetM_variable_sites gives the bases at all 29 variable positions; positions are 1-based.
Two genomes contain multiple mapped sequence types, so genome counts across sequence types cannot be summed. Mapped loci do not establish functional copy number.

chromosomal_verified requires a complete single-contig assembly, chromosomal assignment and no plasmid evidence. Draft chromosome-associated and unresolved classes remain distinct. Same-contig MGE presence does not establish interval overlap or transfer.
Sequences came from 17 SHA256-verified local assemblies and versioned public-contig intervals for 21 other carriers. sequence_source distinguishes these routes.

Equal-cost binary parsimony on the unmasked core tree. Midpoint results and sensitivity across all 301 original edge roots are shown. Root states were free for the reported primary/sensitivity summaries. Gain bounds refer to equally parsimonious minimum-total-change reconstructions; they are conditional estimates, not observed transfer events. Root-absent/present checks are retained in the analysis archive.

tet(M) CDS references GU479464.1 (American, ADF36620.1) and GU479466.1 (Dutch, ADF36634.1), verified from GenBank records and Pachulec and van der Does (2010), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0009962. Values are whole-CDS nucleotide identities. At the 68 reference-discriminating positions every sequence type contains both reference alleles. These profiles remain unresolved; gene-reference similarity does not assign plasmid backbone type.

Profiles are described from nucleotide identity and reference-discriminating sites without imposing a new typing cutoff. Mixed_reference_profile denotes both American-reference and Dutch-reference alleles at those sites; it does not by itself prove recombination. Five short fragments were not typed.

Versioned public contig windows extend up to 30 kb on each side, clipped at contig ends. Every mapped tet(M) interval exactly matches the previously verified sequence. TBLASTN 2.13.0+ searched non-tet(M) reference proteins from U09422.1, GU479464.1 and GU479466.1 at E<=1e-5, >=30% amino-acid identity and >=70% reference-protein coverage. Nearby collinear HSP coverage was combined. Short ORF6/ORF10 matches alone do not identify an intact Tn916-like element.

Four windows lack public CDS annotations but remain evaluable by translated sequence search. Fourteen loci have <2 kb on at least one side. Neither absence of a qualifying match nor absence of a complete backbone in the available window establishes immobility or excludes divergent/fragmented elements. Reference self-controls recovered 75/76 protein queries; the undetected query was a 15-aa partial MarR fragment, not a transfer marker.
